brief.product: The house look in the brown direction: terracotta, warm greys and a serif for titles. One of the two directions being chosen between, and the one to hold against the marketing blue.
brief.notes: Nothing here was invented. Every decision is Northline's except the shell, the name and the sign-in copy, which are Dashcore's so the comparison is between two looks rather than between two companies. Sidebar because the blue direction is sidebar, and a shell difference would read as a design difference.

accent.why: Northline's terracotta, brought over as it stands. Its hue is 20 degrees, inside the zone 04 reserves for danger and warning, which a brand colour in the brief is allowed to override. That override is cheap for one client and dear for a fleet: this would be the primary button in fifteen apps, sitting beside real warning states in the same warm register. Look at the Components screen before choosing it.

temperature.why: Warm greys sit beside terracotta without either of them looking dirty. It is also the clearest difference from the blue direction, which is cool.

pairing.why: Hanken Grotesk with Newsreader, as Northline has it. The serif shows on page titles, sign-in headlines and stat values, which is where this direction reads as considered rather than as an admin tool.

radius.why: The same step as the blue direction, so radius is not one of the things telling them apart.

density.why: The same as the blue direction, for the same reason.

motif.why: Also the same as the blue direction. Two directions that differ in colour and type are a comparison; two that differ in everything are two screenshots.

copy.headline: One standard, every Dashcore app.
copy.tagline: Sign in to see how close each one is.
copy.why: Word for word the blue direction's copy. It is the same product, and copy that moved between the two would be a difference nobody is choosing.
